history.period: c. 10th-11th century CE (Kerala Tourism; murals and carvings dated 15th-16th century)
history.summary: Hindu Krishna temple at Trichambaram, 5 km south of Taliparamba. Mentioned in the 11th-century Sanskrit kavya Mushikavamsha, making it one of North Malabar's oldest temples. The two-storeyed sanctum houses Krishna triumphant after the killing of Kamsa, in ferocious (Raudra) posture; worship is avoided at dawn and nivedhyam is offered immediately on opening. It is called 'North Guruvayoor' as the northward counterpart of Guruvayoor. No elephants are allowed inside, recalling the legend of Kamsa's elephant sent to kill Krishna. The tank Durga shrine is counted among the 108 Durgalayas of ancient Kerala.

name: Trichambaram Temple
town_description: Taliparamba is a historic town in Kannur district of North Malabar, on the banks of the Kuppam River about 20 km north of Kannur city. One of the oldest settlements in the region with roots in the Kolathunadu kingdom, it is famed as a temple town - home to the Rajarajeshwara Temple, one of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, as well as Trichambaram. The town sits on National Highway 66.

travel.road: Thaliparamba bus stand ~1.6 km; on NH 66, ~20 km from Kannur

visitor_information.best_time: March (temple festival season); October-March in general
